customer_question: Which Host Stack QDID should our module's registration Include, given the specific firmware our module datasheet documents?
question_variants: How do we know which Host Stack QDID actually matches our module's firmware?
Is any QDID from the same chip vendor an acceptable match, or does it need to be the exact firmware version?
Where do we find the firmware version our module actually uses?
actual_issue: The product's registration needed to Include a Host Stack QDID corresponding to the exact SoftDevice firmware version actually used by the module, rather than just any QDID associated with the general chip platform, and this needed to be verified against the module vendor's own documentation.
plain_english_explanation: A Bluetooth chip's software stack (the SoftDevice, in this case) comes in different specific versions, and each version has its own separate certification record. Just picking any certification record from the same general chip family isn't good enough -- you need to find the exact one that matches the specific firmware file your module's datasheet says it actually uses, otherwise the registration wouldn't accurately reflect what's really running on the product.
consultant_answer: The Host Stack Included alongside the module's Controller-level reference references the QDID corresponding to the SoftDevice file (s140_nrf52_7.2.0_softdevice.hex) documented on page 11 of the Kaga FEI module's datasheet -- specifically the QDID registered as 'S140 End Product v5.1.' This was identified by cross-referencing the exact SoftDevice firmware version specified in the module vendor's own datasheet against the QDID's actual registered firmware version, rather than assuming any S140-family QDID would be an acceptable match.
decision_logic: When selecting a Host Stack QDID to Include with a module's registration, cross-reference the exact SoftDevice or firmware version documented in the module vendor's own datasheet against the QDID's actual registered firmware version, since different firmware versions within the same chip family have separate QDIDs and are not interchangeable.
final_recommendation: Before Including a Host Stack QDID with a module's registration, check the module vendor's datasheet for the exact firmware/SoftDevice version it documents, and confirm that version matches the QDID actually being referenced rather than assuming any QDID from the same chip family is acceptable.
risk_if_done_wrong: Including a Host Stack QDID that does not match the module's actual documented firmware version would result in a registration that misrepresents the product's actual implementation.
